description: 40x bypass surface — header / path / method / encoding / protocol tricks that flip 401/403 to 2xx on misconfigured ACLs, reverse proxies, WAFs, and admin route guards.

header_origin_spoof.description: Origin/IP spoofing headers (X-Forwarded-For=127.0.0.1, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL) — bypass IP allow-list ACLs or expose admin routes by forging proxy-trust headers.

probes.description: Trust-proxy header rewrites client IP -> internal -> bypass IP ACL
URL-override header reroutes request to admin endpoint on Symfony/Laravel/IIS proxies

path_normalisation_tricks.description: Trailing slash, ;/, /./, %20, %09, double-slash, .json append — abuse reverse-proxy vs origin path normalisation drift.

probes.description: Trailing slash bypass — proxy ACL exact-matches /admin only
Path-parameter ; confuses Spring / Tomcat / Envoy ACL parsers
Servlet path-traversal style — Tomcat / Spring legacy
Trailing space character bypass — Nginx vs Apache ACL drift
Double-slash bypass — proxy normalises before ACL, origin treats as fresh path

IIS ASP.NET cookieless-session segment: insert /(S(<24-char>))/ before a WAF-blocked .aspx path. IIS strips the segment before routing, so a WAF that does not normalize the path fails to match its rule and the protected page serves. Apply to any 403'd .aspx endpoint (swap AdminPanel.aspx for the target path).

method_override.description: Verb-swap (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS) or X-HTTP-Method-Override on endpoints whose ACL enforces only one verb.

probes.description: Verb swap — ACL only protects GET
Method-override header bypasses verb-based ACL

encoding_bypass.description: Double URL-encoding, UTF-8 overlong sequences, and unicode normalization to bypass WAF pattern matching on path and parameter values.

probes.description: Double URL-encoded ../ — the WAF sees %252e (literal percent-two-five-two-e), the origin decodes twice to ../etc/passwd
UTF-8 overlong encoding of .. — two-byte 0xC0 0xAE decodes to U+002E (dot) on vulnerable parsers (IIS, older Java)
Tomcat path-parameter bypass — semicolon confuses path normaliser. The proxy ACL sees ..;/ (not traversal), Tomcat strips the ;/ and resolves ..
Mixed encoding — literal .. plus single-encoded / (%2f). Some WAFs decode only the first layer.

content_type_bypass.description: Change request Content-Type to evade WAF body-inspection rules. Many WAFs only inspect application/json or x-www-form-urlencoded bodies.

probes.description: text/plain bypasses both CORS preflight AND many WAF body-parsing rules. The origin still parses the body as form or JSON based on content.
EBCDIC charset — WAF parses body as ASCII (no pattern match), but some Java/.NET backends auto-transcode IBM037 to UTF-8 and process the payload.
Multipart body splits payload across parts/boundaries. Some WAFs inspect only the first part or fail to reassemble correctly.
Swap JSON to form-urlencoded on API endpoints. If the WAF inspects only JSON bodies and the backend auto-parses form data, the payload evades inspection.

http_version_bypass.description: HTTP version tricks — some WAFs only inspect HTTP/1.1 text frames and pass HTTP/0.9, HTTP/1.0, or HTTP/2 binary frames uninspected.

probes.description: Downgrade to HTTP/1.0 — some WAFs and proxies only hook HTTP/1.1 processing. Connection: close header may also bypass keep-alive analysis.
HTTP/0.9 has no headers — WAFs that rely on header-based rules cannot inspect the request. Requires raw TCP (send_raw_request).
Cleartext HTTP/2 upgrade (h2c) — WAFs that inspect only HTTP/1.1 text miss the binary H2 frames. Use with h2c-smuggling payload.

chunked_encoding_bypass.description: Transfer-Encoding: chunked to split payloads across chunk boundaries, evading WAF pattern-matching that inspects the body as a single buffer.

probes.description: Split SQL keyword across chunk boundary — 'UNION ' in chunk 1, 'SELECT' in chunk 2. WAF sees two fragments, neither matches the UNION SELECT rule.
Duplicate TE headers — the proxy uses the first (chunked), the WAF uses the second (identity) or vice versa, causing desync in body parsing.
Leading tab before 'chunked' — some WAFs fail to normalise whitespace in the TE value and fall back to Content-Length parsing, while the origin accepts it as chunked.

ip_rotation_bypass.description: Source-IP spoofing via trusted-proxy headers — when the WAF or rate-limiter reads client IP from a header instead of the TCP socket, spoofing the header evades IP-based blocks.

probes.description: Triple IP-spoof header stack — covers the three most common proxy-trust headers. If any one is used for rate-limit or IP ACL, the block is evaded.
Cloudflare/Akamai-specific IP headers — True-Client-IP (Akamai), CF-Connecting-IP (Cloudflare). If the origin trusts these without verifying they came from the CDN, IP ACLs are bypassable.
Random IP in XFF to evade per-IP rate limiting. Each request appears from a different source. Use concurrent_requests with rotating XFF.

waf_fingerprint.description: Identify the WAF product by sending a known-blocked payload and analysing the block response. Knowing the WAF guides which bypass techniques to try.

probes.description: Send a basic XSS payload as a query parameter. The WAF's block page or response headers reveal the product: Cloudflare (cf-ray, __cfduid), Akamai (AkamaiGHost), Imperva/Incapsula (incap_ses_, visid_incap_), AWS WAF (x-amzn-requestid), F5 BigIP (BigIP, TS cookie), ModSecurity (Mod_Security), Sucuri (X-Sucuri-ID).
Check response headers on a clean request for WAF fingerprints: CF-Ray (Cloudflare), X-Sucuri-ID (Sucuri), X-CDN (various), Server header containing product names.
